Execute .task/dependable-portions-slice1/next-slice-prompt.md using parallel agents.

Deliver exactly one slice: explicit absolute-use relationships for ordinary URL/photo intake and guarded ingredient/step Save.

- canonical-ingredient-correction: 2.2, 3.2, 4.1 (integration/qualification subsets).

Prerequisites: recipe-view-redesign contains accepted commit 0ee175e45b38407b87c8a562c2d2f086292464e0, deployed as DV operation 7efa8202-e5d9-463d-802e-cd26ccc561d6. Preserve subsequent commits and unrelated work.

Acceptance: preserve C01–C06, C12–C19/C46; qualify C03/C45. Run actual URL/photo workflows including both categorization processors, guarded edits, Cook refresh/state retention and grocery acceptance. Run task prepare then task verify on stable source, real integration checks, hosted verification and exact-commit DV acceptance.

Exclude other new role producers, async AI, library conversion, deferred bilingual/Similar work, unrelated grocery/CI repairs, reset/reseed and production. Keep unfinished aggregates open and selective-ingredient-repair superseded/unimplemented.

Commit and DV deployment are explicitly authorized. Commit only completed owned work; push as needed, deploy that exact commit using established data-preserving recovery procedures, verify images/version/health/user behavior, and integrate accepted commits into recipe-view-redesign.

Stop after this single accepted DV slice. Report SHA, deployment identity, evidence, lifecycle dispositions and limitations. Provide one ready-to-paste successor prompt carrying these commit, DV and next-prompt requirements. Do not launch the successor.

I’ll read the slice prompt and repository guidance, confirm the starting state, then assign the three parallel ownership areas. I’ll carry this single slice through verification, commit, and exact-commit DV acceptance, preserving unrelated work.

The checkout is clean on `recipe-view-redesign` at `b7054b60`, which contains accepted commit `0ee175e4`. I’m using the OpenSpec apply skill for `scale-cooking-step-ingredients` and `canonical-ingredient-correction`, limited to the selected task subsets. Next I’ll check the prior evidence and lifecycle state before assigning implementation.

The prior record identifies DV operation `7efa8202-e5d9-463d-802e-cd26ccc561d6` as accepted, with its failed attempts and limitations retained. The selected absolute-use work is active; whole-use, projection, guarded Save, categorization, and recovery hold are foundations to preserve. Other role producers, later intake channels, library conversion, and bilingual/Similar work remain deferred. Selective ingredient repair remains superseded and unimplemented.

I’ll assign B the producer and unit tests, A the Save/publication integration and PostgreSQL tests, and C the independent preservation and recovery review. I’ll own browser/contracts integration, lifecycle records, final checks, commit, and DV. C will review the prerequisite gates while the writers establish the test baseline.

The existing Save and publication hooks already call the relationship producer and validator, so this may need no new integration mechanism or API shape. B is writing the producer regression tests; A is extending the real PostgreSQL and workflow cases. I’ll preserve the existing whole-use browser journey and add a separate absolute-use variant.

I’m also applying the Next.js QA guidance to the browser acceptance work. C’s prerequisite review has found no blocker so far.

The missing producer behavior now has intended-red evidence: six unit cases and two real PostgreSQL cases found no absolute-use binding before implementation. B’s first implementation passes the producer suite; additional dependency cases are still being checked.

The PostgreSQL red run captured the expected failures, but concurrent source edits invalidated its final content-stability record. I’ll retain that record and run the green and combined gates on stable source.

B’s producer and allocation suite passes: 137 tests, zero skips. In A’s first PostgreSQL green run, Save, ambiguity, and forged-proof rejection passed; the import case failed because the new fixture ran categorization before hero publication. A has corrected the fixture to the established workflow order.

I’ll prepare the complete path set, then freeze source for the database and combined gates. The existing API already supports the absolute-use payload, so no client regeneration is currently needed.

The broader PostgreSQL run passed 139 cases and failed one new fixture case. Its hero receipt used raw JSON where the publication chain requires normalized JSON. A will correct that receipt and tighten the forged-proof test so it proves the intended validator rejected the payload.

I’ll stop the early repository check, retain its output, then prepare and rerun the changed source boundary. No production guard needs changing.

C’s independent review found no reportable source defects. The recovery preflight also restored a fresh read-only DV snapshot: all 31 tables and 1,427 files matched. On the disposable copy, the deployed-image control changed only the previously known derived timestamps.

DV is unchanged. The corrected focused database run is underway; the real browser variants and stable combined gate come next, followed by exact-commit hosted and DV checks.

The real whole-use and absolute-use browser variants now pass all six journeys, including URL/photo categorization, guarded edits, Cook refresh, and groceries. I’m adding a stronger browser assertion that the refreshed checklist shows 375 g, since the absolute step stays at 75 g across the total correction.

The first browser launch failed because I omitted the CI support scripts from the isolated copy. That setup failure is retained; the application source needed no change.

The canonical publication, editing, and recovery checks passed: 140 PostgreSQL cases, zero skips. The combined gate has also passed all 2,029 frontend unit tests and is running browser impact checks. C’s final prepared-source review found no reportable defects.

Prepared-serving preservation is still running separately. Commit, hosted verification, and DV deployment remain pending.

I found that the repository browser check was reusing a pre-existing production server on port 3000. That run cannot establish current-source acceptance. I’ll preserve it as unqualified, leave the user’s server untouched, and rerun the verifier against an owned production build on a separate port.

The separate native/browser and PostgreSQL checks already used isolated resources and remain valid.

The additional prepared/serving check passed: 94 PostgreSQL cases, including current-content corrections at recorded six portions and preserved receipt/count state. Together with the 140 canonical/edit/recovery cases, that gives 234 real database passes with zero skips.

The full verifier is now running browser checks against the owned production build. The existing server on port 3000 remains untouched.

The production browser sweep hit the Search-to-planner navigation case previously recorded as intermittent. I’m retaining the first-failure evidence and waiting for the configured retry and final suite result.

The slice’s six required live browser journeys passed without retries. I won’t expand this work into an unrelated navigation repair.

The remaining local gate is the full production browser sweep. Source is still frozen, and the remote `recipe-view-redesign` branch still matches the starting commit.

After the gate passes, I’ll review and commit the twelve owned paths, then build and verify the exact commit for hosted and DV acceptance. The successor prompt is drafted but has not been launched.

The browser sweep is still running with source frozen. It has reported one first-failure diagnostic so far: the recorded Search navigation case. I’ll retain the final retry outcome with the suite result; the six required live journeys and 234 database cases already passed separately.

The twelve owned paths add bounded producer behavior, acceptance coverage, and lifecycle records. They add no API shape or migration.

The stable repository gate passed: `01d16aefb5a54ba0b65fc2eb3b3d81fa`. It recorded 996 browser passes and one known Search navigation case that passed on its configured retry, plus 98 conditional skips. The separate required checks passed without skips or retries: 234 PostgreSQL cases and six live browser journeys.

I’ll commit the twelve reviewed paths on `dependable-portions-slice-2`, then run exact-commit hosted and DV acceptance before integrating it back into `recipe-view-redesign`.

Commit `780327550ebbe9e34afa13ccbfb07cec46d0b4e5` is signed and pushed on `dependable-portions-slice-2`. Its twelve files match the tested content, and the worktree is clean.

Exact API, PWA, and migration image builds are running, and hosted CI has been triggered. DV still runs the prior accepted commit. Next I’ll rehearse the candidate against the disposable snapshot.
